blocks.text: Many plant cells are totipotent: a single cell can form a new plant, so biologists can grow a whole plant from one transgenic cell. The main purposes of transgenic plants are:

items: Insect resistance: genes of Bacillus thuringiensis, a soil bacterium, have been put into many plants (cotton, rice, maize, potato, tomato, brinjal, cauliflower, cabbage and others); they make proteins that kill insect pests but, the book says, do not harm useful insects.
Herbicide resistance: many crops have been made resistant to glyphosate, a herbicide.

Better nutrition: transgenic 'golden rice' for areas short of dietary iron and vitamin A. The book says genes from beans, the fungus Aspergillus and wild rice were added to raise iron content, and genes for beta-carotene (the precursor of vitamin A) from daffodil.
Biopharmaceuticals: GMO plants and plant cells make cytokines, hormones, antibodies, enzymes and vaccines.

blocks.alt: A flow from left to right: a rod-shaped soil bacterium, Bacillus thuringiensis, with a red gene; the Bt gene on its own; a plant cell holding the gene in its nucleus; a young transgenic plant; and a caterpillar labelled 'eats leaf, dies'. A note below lists crops with Bt genes.
blocks.caption: A Bt gene makes plants insect-resistant (original diagram after Figure 20.7).
blocks.long_description: Many plant cells are totipotent, so a whole plant can be grown from one transgenic cell. Genes of the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis have been put into cotton, rice, maize, potato, tomato, brinjal, cauliflower, cabbage and other plants. The plants make proteins that kill the insect pests that eat them; the book notes that these proteins do not harm other useful insects.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Each year, according to the book, iron deficiency affects 1.4 billion women, and vitamin A deficiency kills 670,000 children and causes 500,000 cases of irreversible childhood blindness.

blocks.title: About golden rice
blocks.text: The name 'golden rice' refers to the beta-carotene (vitamin A) rice, whose grains are yellow. The iron-rich rice made with genes from beans, Aspergillus and wild rice was a related, separate line.

blocks.prompt: Why is it easier to make a transgenic plant than a transgenic animal from one cell?
blocks.explanation: Many plant cells are totipotent: one transformed cell can be grown into a whole plant.

items: Totipotent plant cells regrow whole transgenic plants.
Bt crops kill pests; glyphosate-resistant crops; golden rice for vitamin A (and iron-rich rice).
